summary.headline: Birla Corp Q1 FY27: realisations hit by soft Central India trade prices and lower incentives; Q2 cost up INR70-80/t sequentially, FY27 EBITDA guidance not reiterated.
summary.overview: Management said the quarter was hurt by being at high utilisation in trade and blended cement, where prices did not rise, while gains came from non-trade, industrial and OPC segments where the company has little exposure. Central India prices stayed soft, and the company's dependence on that region rose with Kundanganj Line 3. Reported realisation fell about INR40/t sequentially, which management attributed mainly to lower incentives (INR33 crore vs INR60 crore in Q4) and year-end discounts; excluding these, it said realisation rose INR80/t. Costs rose on fuel and geopolitical factors, with a further INR70-80/t increase expected in Q2. Management kept earlier FY27 capex (INR900 crore), net debt and growth guidance, but declined to comment on full-year EBITDA.

segments.commentary: Management said the company is about 85% blended and over 80% trade; trade prices stayed flat or rolled back in the last month of the quarter, with Central India soft for about a year.

segments.name: Non-trade / OPC / industrial
segments.commentary: Non-trade prices recovered significantly, especially in North and East, but the company's non-trade share is low so the gain had only marginal impact. Company has deliberately de-focused from OPC.

segments.commentary: Current capacity about 43-44 MW, rising to about 50 MW with pipeline projects; Maihar Line 2 expected to add 17-18 MW.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 cost expected to rise INR70-80/t sequentially, mainly fuel and geopolitical factors.
FY27 capex guidance of INR900 crore maintained; management said significant capex step-up expected in FY28.
Peak net debt guidance (about INR4,000 crore, below 2.5x net debt/EBITDA) maintained; year-end FY27 net debt guided around INR2,000 crore.
Incentive for FY27 expected at INR130-135 crore including Mukutban and Kundanganj.
Volume growth guidance (6-7% or industry-level) maintained, but management declined to give full-year EBITDA view, saying it was premature and hopeful for price recovery.
Expansion to 27.6 MTPA by FY29 described as on track; Bikram coal use to rise to 1.2 lakh t this year and 3.5 lakh t next year.
risks_watch: Trade price recovery in Central India: management said it may revisit marketing strategy if larger players do not raise trade prices.
Q2 cost step-up of INR70-80/t from fuel and diesel; geopolitical cost pressure of INR150/t already in Q1.
Monsoon delay could carry over into Q3 and affect harvest-linked rural demand.
New capacity additions in Central India (including JP assets ramp-up) could intensify competition in H2.
Rising packaging and other expenses (INR269/t packaging in Q1) and higher mechanical mining costs at Chanderia.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat defensive: management reiterated existing capex, debt and growth guidance but declined to comment on full-year EBITDA or give a Q2 outlook, pointing to uncertainty in monsoon and pricing. It was confident that competition would stay rational and that the company's strategy will not change.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for Q1 data points (Mukutban volume, lead distance, KCal fuel cost, capex, net debt, incentive) and whether FY27 EBITDA per ton would decline YoY given Q2 cost pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: Mukutban volume 7.5 lakh t, total lead distance 335 km, Mukutban lead about 400 km, fuel cost INR1.64/KCal, capex about INR120 crore, net debt INR2,300 crore, incentive INR33 crore. Q2 cost to rise INR70-80/t sequentially; growth guidance maintained; full-year EBITDA too early to comment, hopeful of price recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether FY27 capex, exit net debt and the FY29 27.6 MTPA expansion timeline are unchanged.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guidance of INR900 crore maintained; exit net debt guidance of around INR2,000-odd crore maintained; company on track for 27.6 MTPA expansion by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how the trade/non-trade mix has changed and whether the company will take course correction.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not shifting away from trade or blended cement; if other players do not raise prices in the trade segment it will decide its own marketing strategy and ways to protect margins, which may not involve price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the other expenses increase (INR511 crore to INR551 crore consolidated) and Kundanganj incentive accrual.
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging costs sit in other expenses, and higher own limestone mining due to higher clinker output also contributed; full Kundanganj benefit this year. Total incentive expected about INR130-135 crore including Mukutban and Kundanganj.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether Central India competition from new capacity (JP assets) will intensify in H2 and how pricing will look.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects more rational competition, does not see a price war, expects new entrants (established players) to ramp up sensibly and compete on marketing rather than price; company will stay on its strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how much has been spent on the 27.6 MTPA expansion and whether FY28 capex will rise sharply.
qa_highlights.answer: Spend so far is almost nil on the expansion phase; next phase is order placement. Management said it is slightly premature but there will be a significant increase in FY28 capex.
